formula.title: How profit margin is calculated
formula.body: Your profit margin is the share of the selling price left after all the costs of an order. Add up the costs, subtract them from the selling price to get net profit, then divide net profit by the selling price.

cost.expression: purchase price + shipping + ads + Tallaby fee

example.title: Example: a cotton shirt
example.fee: Tallaby fee ({orderFee} per order at today's exchange rate)

markup.q: What's the difference between margin and markup?
markup.a: Margin is measured against the selling price, and markup against the cost. In the example above the profit is EGP {profit}: that's a {margin} margin on the selling price and a {markup} markup on the cost.

healthy.q: What's a good profit margin for an online store?
healthy.a: It depends on your category and ad costs. What matters is that the margin stays positive after every cost, with room for a discount code or a return without making a loss.

shipping.q: Do I include shipping if the customer pays for it?
shipping.a: No. Enter only the part you cover, such as free delivery or the gap between what the customer pays and what you pay the shipping company.

ads.q: How do I work out my ad cost per order?
ads.a: Divide your total ad spend over a period by the orders from the same period. For example, EGP 3,000 ÷ 50 orders = EGP 60 per order.

saved.q: Are the numbers I enter saved?
saved.a: Only on your device, so they're there when you come back. Nothing is sent to a server. Press Reset to go back to the example figures.

fee.q: How does the calculator count the Tallaby fee?
fee.a: The Free plan's fee is {orderFee} per order at today's exchange rate, taken from your store wallet, while your orders and prices stay in pounds. So the calculator counts {fee} EGP per order. Pro costs {pro} a month with no order fee, so it doesn't count against a single order.

costs.title: What goes into an online store's cost?
costs.lead: The cost of an online store in Egypt isn't one number. These are the items you pay each month, and who sets each one.

items.title: Platform fees
items.body: On Tallaby: {orderFee} per order on the Free plan, or {pro} a month on Pro with no order fees.

items.title: Payment gateway
items.body: If you take cards through Paymob or Kashier, the gateway charges its fees for your account. Cash on delivery has no gateway fee.

items.title: Domain
items.body: Optional. Your store starts on a free link; for your own domain you pay a registrar each year.

items.title: Shipping
items.body: The customer usually pays it with the order, and you pay your carrier or rider as agreed.

items.title: Apps
items.body: Some apps have a cost, such as order notification emails. You see the cost in your dashboard before turning one on.

items.title: Ads
items.body: The biggest item for most sellers, and yours to set. See its effect on profit with the profit margin calculator.

store-cost-calculator.faqTitle: Questions about the cost of an online store

total.q: How much does it cost to create an online store in Egypt?
total.a: On Tallaby there's no setup fee and no monthly fee on the Free plan, and you pay {orderFee} per order. Add your gateway's fees if you take cards, and a domain if you want your own.

free.a: Creating a store is free. The Free plan has no monthly fee, and you pay {orderFee} for each order you get.

pro.a: When your Free order fees add up to more than Pro's monthly {pro}. Enter your order count in the calculator to see which costs less.

domain.q: Do I need to buy a domain?
domain.a: No. Your store starts on a free tallaby.com link, and connecting your own domain is optional and on both plans.

gateway.a: Paymob or Kashier set it for your account, and Tallaby takes no share of sales. Type your account's rate in the calculator.

shipping.q: Why doesn't the calculator include shipping?
shipping.a: The customer usually pays shipping with the order, and it costs the same on both plans. To see shipping's effect on profit, use the profit margin calculator.

topUp.q: How do I pay Tallaby's fees?
topUp.a: Fees come out of your store wallet, which you top up in EGP from {topUpMin}. You need a first top-up within {days} days or when your first order arrives, whichever comes first, to keep seeing new orders.

toolsHub.explainerTitle: Why work it out before you sell?
toolsHub.explainer: Most sellers know their buying price, but few add up shipping, ads, platform fees and card fees together. These tools do it for you: the store cost calculator tells you what you pay each month and which plan costs less, and the profit margin calculator tells you what you keep from each order. Your numbers stay in your browser and are sent nowhere.
